findings.summary: The requested behaviour is built only as a hook. No real records are committed from the landing queue, so production record ordering is unchanged at every bound.
findings.evidence: The only definition of Steps::commit_records in the codebase is the default `Ok(())` at drain.rs:633. A grep finds no override in the real Athena-backed Steps, and the only overrides are the test stub `Recording` in tests/drain.rs. The candidate's own design note says 'Not built here: the real steps keep the default. Today `go` still commits a job's closing files and its score and outcome records at close (land_or_block in run/close.rs), before the job joins the landing queue, so those commits follow close order.' The request says 'commit records from the landing queue after each landing'. The user-accepted reading says 'the drain commits each landed job's records from the landing queue right after its landing', and its assumption expects the producer to wire the commit to the real landing step. The cited design (async-drain.md section 8 and build job 8) says each job writes its records locally without committing them and the queue commits them after landing. None of that happens in a real drain. The tests commit synthetic priority records from a stub, not the job's real records. Build job 9 depends on job 8, yet the essential move of the close-time commit is deferred to unnamed 'later work'. Simpler, correct alternative: have the real steps defer the close-time records commit for a job that will land, and commit them in the real Steps::commit_records override. Pin bound 1 with the existing real-steps tests.
findings.location: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:633 (default hook, no real override); docs/design/async-drain.md:236-242

findings.summary: Build job 8's second half, 'confirm the append-only conflict rule', is explicitly left undone.
findings.evidence: async-drain.md:221 says the month-shard conflict reading 'is to be confirmed by build job 8 before it is relied on', and job 8 at line 344-345 says 'confirm the append-only conflict rule'. The candidate's note at line 241 says 'The month-shard conflict reading is not confirmed', so the doc's requirement is still open after the job meant to close it.

findings.summary: The ordering tests depend on wall-clock sleeps.
findings.evidence: three_in_flight uses run times of 50, 150 and 300 ms, plus a 5 s spin barrier and a 100 ms hold in commit_records. On a heavily loaded runner the run-end order could shift. The tests would then fail loudly (assert ended == 'c a b'), not pass silently, so this is a flakiness risk rather than a false pass.

summary: The candidate adds a `Steps::commit_records` hook that `Drain::land` calls right after a successful landing, while the job still holds the head of the landing queue. It adds five tests that drive `drain_concurrent` with a stub committing real records through the committer. I ran the new tests with --nocapture: three jobs in flight, landing sequence c a b, records sequence c a b, each records commit directly after its own landing. The git diff in the fixture repo shows only added files, the earlier record is byte-identical, and the rejected job gets no record. All 145 integration tests and 47 drain unit tests pass, no existing test was edited, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. All six criteria are met as written. The verdict is still fail. The real steps keep the no-op default, so in a real drain no records are committed from the landing queue: `go` still commits a job's records at close, before landing, in close order. The candidate's own CHANGELOG and design note say so. The request, the accepted reading and design section 8 / build job 8 all ask for the actual records commit to move into the queue slot and for the append-only conflict rule to be confirmed. Neither is done, and the conflict rule is explicitly left unconfirmed. What landed is the ordering hook and its proof with a stub, not the records commit ordering the job asks for.
